text.p: MUNICH, Germany, March 25 - German luxury car-maker Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) said on Tuesday it boosted 1996 profits and was out to increase its earnings power in the current year.
BMW said 1996 profit, according to the widely-used German DVFA accounting standard, rose to 959 million marks ($568.6 million) from 795 million.
It has already reported 1996 sales up 13.3 percent to 52 billion marks, with net profits up 18.5 percent to 820 million marks.
"The BMW group will make the most of its opportunities to continue to increase its productivity and strengthen its earning power," the company said in its annual financial report.
Losses at its British Rover unit narrowed to 279 million marks in 1996 from 335 million in 1995.
The company said it expected demand to grow slowly in Europe this year and that markets in North America as well as Japan would stagnate.
"After strong growth in 1996, the trend in BMW car sales should stabilise at a high level."
